title: R Graphs
text:
On Aug. 17th through the 21st I took a week long crash course on how to use R for Data Science.

library(tidyverse)

ggplot(
  data = mpg, 
  mapping = aes(
    x = cty,
    y = hwy
  )
)+ geom_point()








This is great, but one thing we learned about is the importance of clear labels using the lab functions.

library(tidyverse)

ggplot(
  data = mpg, 
  mapping = aes(
    x = cty,
    y = hwy
  )
)+ geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth() + 
  labs(
    x = "City Milage",
    y = "Highway Milage", 
    title = "City vs Highway"
  )

`geom_smooth()` using method = 'loess' and formula = 'y ~ x'

title: Salem Web-Blog: A Small Business Digital Growth Initiative
Salem Web-Blog: A Small Business Digital Growth Initiative
text:
Overview
Salem Custom Screen Printing is a small t-shirt screening business, and I’m building its website as a Small Business Digital Growth Initiative. The site is a blog-style home for the business’s designs, sales, and events, and it’s live here: Salem Blog.

title: Salem Web-Blog: A Small Business Digital Growth Initiative
text:
More Than a Client
This isn’t a paid job, and the business owner isn’t just a client to me. I chose to take this on because I want to see Salem grow, and because I wanted to build something real for someone I care about. That also means we talk openly: the owner tells me what the business needs, I translate it into the site, and I show progress along the way so the project stays tied to what actually matters to them.

title: Salem Web-Blog: A Small Business Digital Growth Initiative
text:
The Problem
Salem needed a stronger online presence to promote the brand and keep customers coming back. Designs, sales, and events were shared in conversations and photos, with no central place for people to see what Salem offers.

title: Salem Web-Blog: A Small Business Digital Growth Initiative
text:
What I’ve Built So Far

A live, branded website built with Quarto and hosted on GitHub Pages, featuring Salem’s logo and a clean homepage.
A blog with four posts: the business’s mission, a recap of the Rooted event, a Family Christmas Bundle sale, and an October sale.
Organization for visitors: posts are tagged by category (Mission, Rooted, Sale) and can be sorted by date or title.
An About page and a “Join the Salem list” page where visitors can sign up for updates.
Social links to Salem’s Instagram and Facebook.
A complete Solution Design Worksheet mapping the full system: pages, data, automations, AI features, third-party services, hosting, a system diagram, and a step-by-step walkthrough of the subscriber flow.

I started the project in Posit Cloud and moved it to VS Code with Git and GitHub, so I can version my work and push updates directly to the live site.



The main page on the Salem site

title: Salem Web-Blog: A Small Business Digital Growth Initiative
text:
My Role
I’m the sole developer and maintainer. I handle the design, the code, the publishing, and all communication with the business owner, from gathering content to showing progress and getting feedback.

title: Salem Web-Blog: A Small Business Digital Growth Initiative
text:
Challenges and What I Learned

Moving from Posit Cloud to VS Code
Turning the owner’s needs into a plan: Working through the design worksheet forced me to ask what the business actually needs, such as customer contact info for deals and news, rather than just what would be fun to build.

title: Salem Web-Blog: A Small Business Digital Growth Initiative
text:
What’s Next
Based on my design, the next steps are:

Email subscriptions with automation: When someone subscribes, an automation will save their info to a Google Sheet, add them to a newsletter list, send a welcome email, and notify the owner. Every email will include an unsubscribe link, and new blog posts will be emailed automatically through the site’s RSS feed.
AI-powered helpers: A customer FAQ assistant (minimum orders, pricing, how to order) and a quote assistant that turns a plain-English request into a readable order.
Customization and ordering: Letting customers browse and customize shirts, with payment, and eventually a drag-and-drop designer.
Social media integration and an expanded page structure as the library of designs and events grows.

title: The Relationship Between U.S. Stock Market Returns and Treasury Bond Yields: A Statistical Analysis
text: This project examines the relationship between the U.S. stock market and the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield from 2000 through 2026. The S&P 500 is used to represent stock-market performance, while the 10-year Treasury yield represents conditions in the U.S. bond market. Historical S&P 500 data were obtained through Yahoo Finance, while Treasury yield data were collected from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED). Using R, I analyze the relationship between daily S&P 500 returns and changes in the 10-year Treasury yield, with particular attention to how this relationship changed during the 2008–2009 Financial Crisis and the 2020 COVID-19 market shock.

title: The Relationship Between U.S. Stock Market Returns and Treasury Bond Yields: A Statistical Analysis
section: How did the relationship between U.S. stock-market returns and changes in 10-year Treasury yields differ between the 2008–2009 financial crisis and the 2020 COVID-19 market shock?

The relationship between S&P 500 returns and changes in 10-year Treasury yields strengthened during periods of major financial stress. This is reflected in the increase in R² from 0.082 during 2000–2026 to 0.1495 during the 2008–2009 Financial Crisis and 0.2303 during the 2020 COVID-19 period. Thus, changes in Treasury yields explained a greater proportion of the variation in daily S&P 500 returns during both crises.

# R Data Science Portfolio

A portfolio of data science projects and analyses created with R. This site highlights my approach to exploring data, communicating insights, and building reproducible workflows.

## About

I use data analysis and visualization to turn raw data into clear, useful insights. This portfolio brings together selected projects, code, and findings.

## Featured Work

This portfolio brings together multiple projects and analyses that demonstrate a range of data science skills, including:

- Data cleaning and preparation
- Exploratory data analysis
- Statistical analysis and modeling
- Data visualization and reporting
- Communicating insights through reproducible workflows

Each project includes context, methodology, and key results where applicable.

## Other Projects in This Portfolio

The portfolio includes work from several project areas beyond a single analysis track, such as:

- **Stock-Bond Analysis** — exploring market relationships and portfolio-oriented analysis
- **Salem-Web-Blog** — combining storytelling with data-informed reporting
- **cool_ggplot_work** — experimenting with advanced visual design and chart communication
- **myDog** — applying exploratory analysis and data presentation to a personal dataset

These projects show how the same core R-based workflow can be applied across different topics, datasets, and communication styles.

## Tools

- **R** for data wrangling, analysis, and visualization
- **RStudio** for development and reporting
- R packages selected for each project's needs

## Getting Started

To explore the project files, clone this repository:

```bash
git clone <repository-url>
Open the relevant project files in RStudio. Install any packages listed in the individual project instructions before running the analysis.
